newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says Boracay beach is safe for swimmers.
newsitem.headline: Manila says Boracay beach is safe for swimmers.

text.p: The Philippines said on Friday that its most famous beach resort, earlier declared by the country's environment chief as an ecological disaster, was safe after all.
"It is now safe to swim in Boracay," a joint statement issued by Environment and Natural Resources Secretary Victor Ramos and Tourism Secretary Mina Gabor said.

The two met in a special meeting in the presidential palace after Gabor and local officials of Boracay island raised a howl of protest over a statement by Ramos saying the island was contaminated with coliform bacteria which can cause diarrhoea, typhoid and skin diseases.
Boracay, famous for its sparkling white sand and clear blue seas, draws about 200,000 foreign tourists every year and hotel owners were terrified their source of revenue would disappear.
Coliform bacteria comes from human wastes leaked into the sea.

"(The) coliform levels were based on samplings and findings between October and December 1996 only. The southwest monsoon with its tidal movements is expected to further enhance the quality of water in Boracay," the statement said.
A monitoring system will be set up to regularly test the quality of water, "and if need be, on a daily basis".
Ramos said what he was referring to as a "disaster" and will need five to 10 years of rehabilitation was the underground water of the island, which had never been used as a potable water source.
